SNACS review rules (v2.6; from authorized examples)

Represent each target as [scene_role, lexical_function]; both labels use p. prefixes. Role is the relation in context; function is the lexical contribution of the adposition or marker. They can match or differ through construal. Choose from complement plus governing predicate/construction, not the preposition alone.

Quantity and partitive of:
- ‘Each of you’ / ‘one of them’: p.QuantityItem/p.Whole, where a quantifying expression denotes a subset/member relative to a set.
- ‘plenty of options’: p.QuantityItem/p.QuantityItem (measure/amount construction; complement is the quantity-bearing item, not a whole set).

Emotion, evaluation, and possession:
- ‘proud/pleased with contributions/that one’: p.Stimulus/p.Topic; the complement evokes the emotion and is its topic.
- Possessive linked to an event noun where possessor is the actor (‘your contributions’, ‘her help’): p.Agent/p.Gestalt.
- Body part possessed by its whole (‘my hair’): p.Whole/p.Gestalt.
- Ordinary ownership (‘your money’, ‘my dogs’, ‘my hooptie’): p.Possessor/p.Possessor. ‘my PA’ as social relation: p.SocialRel/p.Gestalt.

Circumstance and paths:
- ‘Throughout the year’ expressing duration: p.Duration/p.Duration.
- ‘By saying’ when saying is the means of an act: p.Means/p.Means.
- Event/place location (‘at Lovely Nails’, ‘on Military Road’, ‘driving on highway’): p.Locus/p.Locus.
- Destination at an institution (‘went to the school’): p.Org/p.Goal; ordinary motion destination (‘go to station’, ‘went to a surgeon’): p.Goal/p.Goal. Directional movement governs Goal; static location is Locus.
- ‘from perfect’ marks source: p.Source/p.Source.

Other recurring distinctions:
- ‘for’ can be p.Beneficiary/p.Beneficiary for whom an action/service is done; p.Purpose/p.Purpose for intended function (‘things for earrings’, ‘get napkins’, ‘made to suit’); p.ComparisonRef/p.Purpose in ‘too much for daycare’ (degree exceeds comparison standard, construed as purpose). Inspect construction.
- ‘to’ infinitive with intended action is p.Purpose/p.Purpose; ‘to suit me’ likewise purpose. But experiencer complement of adjective (‘important to them’) is p.Experiencer/p.Goal.
- ‘with’ in a characteristic construction (‘crap with/over my hair’) can be p.Characteristic/p.Characteristic.
- ‘like’ in an explicit comparison (‘like driving a new car’) is p.ComparisonRef/p.ComparisonRef; in ‘a surgeon like him’ identity resemblance is p.Identity/p.ComparisonRef.
- ‘on’ with maintenance ‘on my hooptie’ is p.Theme/p.Theme, while ordinary location on a road is Locus.
- ‘at least’ is extent: p.Extent/p.Extent.
- In ‘job of taking care’, of can be p.Identity/p.Identity.
- Genitive ’s on a possessor: ordinary possession p.Possessor/p.Gestalt, while an eventive possessor can be p.Agent/p.Gestalt; beneficiary ’s (e.g. ‘bus boys station’ meaning station serving them) can be p.Beneficiary/p.Possessor.

Always distinguish partitive of (QuantityItem/Whole), stimulus/topic of emotional predicates, and possessive uses. Use Locus for where an event or property holds; use Goal when a directional relation is expressed. For for-phrases, distinguish recipient/beneficiary, purpose, and comparison standard from the governing predicate and construction.
